stem: Impending relapse of leukemia after allogeneic HSCT may be revealed by the monitoring of chimerism. Which of the following findings is not suggestive of relapse?

options.A: Reappearance of recipient cells displaying the immunophenotype of original leukemia
options.B: Increasing recipient chimerism within total leukocytes
options.C: Chimerism finding indicative of graft rejection.
options.D: Increasing donor chimerism within total leukocytes

stem: Which of the following statements regarding EB virus viremia post HSCT was wrong?

options.A: Only occurred in allogeneic HSCT recipients
options.B: Pre‐emptive antiCD20 treatment was recommended in unrelated donor HSCT recipients with EBV viremia
options.C: Patients received unrelated donor HSCT possessed high risk for development of EBV related lymphoproliferative disorder
options.D: There are standardized method of EBV viremia molecular monitoring

stem: Which of the following statement is wrong?

options.A: Patients with chronic GVHD should receive antibiotic prophylaxis targeting encapsulated organisms given for at least as long as immunosuppressive therapy maintained.
options.B: After HSCT, antifungal prophylaxis should be considered in patients with severe GVHD.
options.C: PJP prophylaxis was indicated in allogeneic HSCT recipients from D+1 till D+100 or as long as immunosuppressive therapy is given (e.g., for the treatment or prevention of chronic GVHD).
options.D: HSV prophylaxis was recommended from D+1 to engraftment in allogeneic HSCT recipients receiving myeloablative conditioning

stem: Which of the following statement is wrong?

options.A: CMV viremia can occurred in autologous HSCT recipient.
options.B: Pre‐emptive anti‐CMV therapy was recommended in allo‐HSCT recipients with CMV viremia and grade 2 acute GvHD.
options.C: Foscarnet is an alternative for ganciclovir in the anti‐CMV treatment because no myelosuppression adverse effect reported in its AE profiles.
options.D: Prophylactic mold‐active azoles, and probably echinocandins, are proven to be effective in preventing invasive fungal diseases in allogeneic HSCT.

stem: Which of the following statements about hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is wrong?

options.A: Allogeneic HSCT is a potential curative treatment for AML patients who are primarily refractory to induction therapy.
options.B: If a complete remission could not be achieved after two cycles of conventional dose induction, or one cycle containing high‐dose cytarabine, allogenic HSCT should be pursued if an adequate stem cell donor is ready.
options.C: For AML patients of the ELN favorable risk (e.g. NPM1 mutated, FLT3 wild type) with positive measurable residual disease, HSCT with an adequate donor is indicated.
options.D: To assess the transplant risk, “HCT‐Comorbidity Index” have been validated in the population of AML while “EBMT risk score” has not yet.
options.E: For patients with acute promyelocytic leukemia who had relapsed and then achieved the second complete remission (CR2), autologous HSCT can be considered if in a molecular remission (PML::RARA(‐)).

ebmt_chapters: Ch11 Evaluation and Counseling of Candidates (PDF p131–142)

stem: Which of the following statement about allo-HSCT for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is wrong?

options.A: Allo‐HSCT should not be considered for patients with CML who failed imtatinib but rescued by nilotinib or dasatinib back to chronic phase.
options.B: Allo‐HSCT is recommended for patients in blastic phase after debulking with the 2nd‐or 3rd‐generation of TKI plus induction chemotherapy.
options.C: Compared with CML in the 1st chronic phase (CP), the transplant outcome was not worse in the 2nd CP once the 2nd‐ or 3rd‐generation of TKI rescued those who had progressed to advanced stages.
options.D: For CML patients who received transplant, GvHD after DLI was associated with an at least 2‐fold increase in risk of death as compared with patients without GvHD
options.E: The best sequence of DLI first or TKI first for post‐allo‐HSCT CML relapse has not been defined.

ebmt_chapters: Ch59 Delayed Transfer of Immune Cells or the Art of Donor Lymphocyte Infusion (DLI) 2.0 (PDF p532–540)

stem: Select CORRECT answer from the following statements about minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment in adult ALL.

options.A: The commonly used techniques of MRD assessment include short‐tandem repeat (STR) analysis, fusion gene transcript detection, NGS, and flow cytometry.
options.B: For a young adult ALL of standard risk with significant reduction of MRD after induction and undetectable MRD after consolidation, subsequent transplantation would provide further survival benefit.
options.C: When MRD assessment is not available, transplantation for a young adult in CR1 with suitable donor may provide survival benefit.
options.D: For an adult ALL harboring t(9;22) with MRD being undetectable by RQ‐PCR after consolidation, transplantation is generally not indicated.

ebmt_chapters: Ch72 Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in Adults (PDF p642–650)
Ch57 Monitoring Measurable Residual Disease in ALL and AML (PDF p516–524)

stem: Which of the following statements about HSCT for patients with follicular lymphoma is NOT true?

options.A: Auto‐HSCT should be considered as a first‐line consolidation procedure in patients who achieved first response.
options.B: There is no proven role for purging strategies.
options.C: Auto‐HSCT may cure some patients and is associated with lower toxicity compared to allo‐HSCT.
options.D: RIC allo‐HSCT can act as an effective salvage strategy in patients that relapse after auto‐HSCT.

stem: Which of the followings is NOT an adverse prognostic factor identified in prospective studies for patients with diffuse large B cell lymphoma being treated with auto-HSCT?

options.B: Early relapse (within 12 months of induction therapy).
options.D: Involvement of two or more extranodal sites at relapse.
